title: Prove selected forward helper450 unit row in Lean
body:
Proves the scalar unit output row at register 450 for the complete selected forward word already translated in PR2944. For every initial state on all 1,024 typed registers, including arbitrary private-register contents, the final scalar value at 450 equals its initial value. The concrete theorem supplies `∀ j, S K8.Forward.events 450 j = if j = 450 then 1 else 0`.

The proof reuses the existing 24,757-event word byte-for-byte. Two opposite ADDs restore the helper; kernel-checked target-avoidance predicates establish that their partner is unchanged between them. Checks use the original 97 blocks and do not require a larger Lean stack.

Validation: fresh Lean 4.21 replay and exact axiom audit, three rejected false restoration claims, two positive controls (relabels and row-versus-column separation), and seven Python 3.12 source/arithmetic control groups. The registered replay authenticates the archived kernel receipt and source generation; it does not invoke Lean. Exact commands, environment, and receipts are in the package.

This is a forward scalar-row theorem. The JSON adapter, backward row, isolated dirt column, physical recipes, ownership, and full selected cold replay remain separate obligations. No selected frontier or κ changes.

Credits: Hanson Sun's numeric binding (PR1611), Nick Petalas's complete typed word and label proof (PR2944), Cinna Davis's composition lemma (PR3331), and the retained Lemma G/HPE lineage. New work by Sagar Thakrar with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; separate agent review is not human review.

Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2703#discussioncomment-19007184
